## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Bhaguttheragāthā* (Thag 4.2) is a short poem of the *Theragāthā* in the Khuddaka Nikāya, preserving verses attributed to the elder Bhagu [SuttaCentral]. The text belongs to the *Catukkanipāta* (Book of the Fours), consisting of four verses. SuttaCentral records nine translations in eight modern languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

Text-reuse data identified by DharmaNexus links the poem closely with its canonical commentary in the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (*Dutiyo bhāgo*), which treats the entire sequence of verses (§1.1–4.5), with additional citations found in the *Paṭhamo bhāgo* [DharmaNexus]. Within the *Theragāthā* collection, verses §2.4–4.5 are identical to a passage in the *Rājadattattheragāthā* (Thag 5.1, §4.1–5.5) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also reports an automated cross-language alignment between this text (§0.3–0.4) and the Chinese *Bieyi Za ahan jing* (T 100, fascicle 13) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
